summary: Gone Teton National Forest cabin on Signal Mountain, built 1938, struck by lightning in 1951; the site is now in Grand Teton National Park.

facts.design: Rustic cabin with stone walls, sliding sash on all four sides and a pyramid-shaped wood-shingle roof (Willhite Web)
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com lists it as gone; Forest Lookouts marks it Removed. Neither gives a year.

staffing.status: last recorded lookouts Marie and Bob Baugh, 1951

facts.agency: Grand Teton National Park (built as a Teton National Forest lookout)

visit.trail_note: Willhite Web lists the hiking distance as 'Drive up'; no source describes the site today or current public access

events.note: Teton Forest cabin reported as recently constructed in July 1938

Lookouts Marie and Bob Baugh were on duty at the 1951 lightning strike

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates Ben Sheffield to 1938-1939; Willhite Web says he worked as a lookout in the late thirties and early forties. Both are kept.
A 1938 item gives 7,720 feet; Willhite Web gives 7,731 feet with 7,720 feet in parentheses; firelookout.com gives 7733 feet. The story gives no elevation.
The 1938 items name the Teton National Forest; firelookout.com names Grand Teton National Park for the site. Both are kept.

notes_for_editor: No removal year appears in any source; Forest Lookouts marks it Removed without a date. No source describes remains or current public access. Staffing and elevation conflicts are recorded in resolved_conflicts. The 1955 USGS map caption on the Willhite page was not used. Willhite Web has photos of the lookout but no direct image URL was captured, so no photos are listed. One web search used. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the August 9, 1951 date belongs to the Jackson's Hole Courier item (August 9, 1951 was a Thursday) and the strike is reported as Sunday night with no strike date, so the story no longer dates the strike to August 9. The 7,000-register item is dated January 25, 1939. The drive-up note was reworded so it does not imply the site is open to the public.
